title: SSE chunk-manifest + continuation-token reconnect protocol for safe-toolcall boundaries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a light-weight chunk-manifest and continuation-token exchange layered on top of SSE to provide robust reconnect behavior while preserving function/tool-call and structured-output atomicity. This ticket defines wire hints, checksum strategy, and client/server negotiation for pragmatic compatibility with existing JSONL/legacy consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits a per-chunk manifest envelope for each logical chunk that includes byte-length, semantic-boundary hint, CRC32c checksum, and an opaque continuity token.
Clients can reconnect using an X-Redwood-Resume-Hint header with a continuation token; server uses the token to validate and provide a resume offset or safe-restart decision.
Function/tool-call frames are never split across resumable chunks: either complete call frame appears in the same chunk or server marks chunk as non-resumable and provides safe-fallback guidance.
Compatibility layer passes end-to-end tests that simulate lost mid-chunk connections, byte-truncation, and replayed resume tokens.
Load/latency benchmarks show <5% median latency increase at 95th percentile under typical token sizes (<=512) compared to baseline SSE without manifests.
Implementation includes integration tests, a short migration guide for SDKs, and one runtime feature flag for gradual rollout.
technical_notes: Manifest envelope: single-line JSON prefixed with 'event: manifest' followed by data: <base64(manifest)> per SSE semantics to avoid breaking line-based JSONL parsers.

Manifest fields: version (int), chunk_id (uuid), chunk_len_bytes (int), semantic_hint (one of: 'complete', 'boundary', 'nonresumable'), crc32c (base64), sha256_prefix (first 8 bytes hex) for cross-check, continuation_token (opaque base64) and produced_at (ISO8601).
Continuation token design: server-generated HMACed blob (k=v pairs) containing last_valid_offset, chunk_id, model_version, and expiry_ms. Opaque to clients; server validates on resume.

Resume flow: client reconnects and sends X-Redwood-Resume-Hint: <token>. Server validates token; if token trusted and data present, replies with 200 + header X-Redwood-Resume-Offset: <byte_offset> and starts streaming from the next byte. If token expired or mismatch, server returns header X-Redwood-Resume-Decision: restart or fallback-to-last-good-chunk.

Toolcall safety: when server sees a pending function call boundary inside an incoming chunk, manifest must mark semantic_hint='nonresumable' and server will prefer to drain and mark chunk id as atomic; resume will ask client to restart last operation or switch to idempotent request path.

Compatibility: legacy clients will ignore 'event: manifest' lines and continue consuming data; to help progressive SDKs we provide an opt-in 'manifest-aware' bool in initial SSE handshake (query param ?manifest=true).
risks: Small extra CPU for manifest generation at high QPS - mitigated by sampling manifests for tiny chunks (<64 bytes) or by offloading manifest generation to async worker.

Edge-case: mid-chunk function-call boundary where model produced a multi-part structured result; solution requires server to either mark chunk non-resumable or checkpoint a safe semantic snapshot (higher cost).
Implementation complexity with multiplexed SSE lanes - requires per-lane manifest namespace to avoid cross-stream token confusion.
Security: continuation token replay risk mitigated by short TTL (default 45s), embedded model_version and HMAC key rotation logs.
test_plan: Unit: manifest encode/decode, token HMAC verify/rotate, semantic_hint transitions.
Integration: three-fault scenarios: abrupt disconnect mid-chunk, truncated tail, replayed token; assert client-visible outcome matches acceptance criteria.
Fuzz: generate random chunk boundaries and functioncall annotations to ensure no case where function-call is split and left marked resumable.
Performance: 24h throughput run at production QPS, measure 95/99p latency, CPU overhead and manifest generation cost.
metrics: toolcall_boundary_violations (count) - should be zero in accepted runs
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): enable manifests behind flag on staging for 2 weeks, collect metrics and run synthetic disconnects.
Phase 2 (beta): opt-in SDK clients via ?manifest=true query param; enable for 10% of inbound traffic, monitor resume_success_rate.
Phase 3 (ga): flip feature flag as default for runtime-2025.03 after successful metric thresholds and security review.
Rollback: global flag to disable manifest emission and invalidate tokens by rotating HMAC key.
